final.memo:
Bank of America remains a strong, deposit-funded franchise with a demonstrated ability to earn attractive returns on tangible capital [D01], [D03]. We continue to admire the business, and our view of its long-term competitive position is unchanged [D01].

However, our position has reached a scale where we are subject to significant regulatory reporting requirements due to exceeding the 10% ownership threshold [D08]. Charlie and I have long preferred to operate without the complications that attend these reporting burdens, and we have historically adjusted our holdings to remain just under the 10% limit when ownership approaches those levels [S3]. 

Furthermore, in a market where attractive, reasonably priced opportunities are scarce, maintaining a high level of liquidity is prudent [D08]. By trimming our position, we satisfy the regulatory objective while generating cash to bolster our resources, accepting the 21% tax cost as a necessary component of disciplined capital allocation [S3], [D04]. This is a move of convenience and regulatory management, not a commentary on the underlying quality of the bank's earnings or its management team [D03].
